summary: Eleven experiments finished in 9.5 minutes. The 9-minute synthesis handoff dominated elapsed time, while the two compute-bound experiments fall under the supplied GPU-idle classification; only one appears in the top five, with a rounded duration of 0 minutes.

bottlenecks_identified: The synthesis-only terminal-boundary handoff took 9 of the milestone's 9.5 minutes and was the demonstrated wall-time bottleneck.
GPU engagement was absent while compute-bound work was present. The rounded timing data does not quantify the resulting delay.
Disk-mtime fallback produced 0-minute entries and no phase attribution, so the longest compute phase and its cause are not available.
improvements_suggested: Add monotonic phase timers and reusable checkpoint receipts to the terminal-boundary handoff so unchanged validation work can be skipped safely.
Add a compute-bound startup health check that correlates the task process with GPU utilization and stops or retries a run that remains idle after startup.
Record loaded-model count and dispatcher choice in each compute artifact; select DualGPURunner only when at least two models are loaded concurrently.
Persist sub-minute task and phase durations instead of relying on rounded disk modification times.
top_3_highest_leverage_actions: Checkpoint and phase-time the terminal-boundary handoff.
Gate compute-bound execution on task-correlated GPU engagement.
Emit precise duration, loaded-model-count, and dispatcher receipts for every compute task.
meta_reflection: The fallback reconstructs the milestone total but rounds several listed tasks to 0 minutes and does not expose phase causes. No data available this milestone supports a measured savings estimate or a missed concurrent-model DualGPURunner dispatch.
